patch.value: Preserve .toon extra metadata key order in list output

Native list output sorts extra metadata keys alphabetically (BTreeMap decoding in the item reader), while published PM CLI 2026.10.5 preserves the .toon file order in --full row projections. Verified byte-level against the installed reference: a task with metadata keys zebra, budget, alpha prints alpha/budget/zebra natively but zebra/budget/alpha in the reference. Existing differential fixtures never use non-alphabetical metadata, so this pre-existing divergence at HEAD is invisible to the current PR #60 suite; the new float-metadata differential test works around it with alphabetical fixture keys. Fixing this requires order-preserving metadata decoding and may affect .toon write-back formatting and history hashes.
Full-row list output preserves .toon file metadata order byte-identically against published PM CLI 2026.10.5

value.author: pi-rust-greptile2
value.text: Reproduction evidence from the PR #60 review follow-up: a synthetic task with extra metadata zebra: 1, budget: 30.0, alpha: 2 (in that file order) was read with list --json --full by both real executables. The reference emits zebra/budget/alpha; native emits alpha/budget/zebra. All float values match after the JS number formatting fix, so this is purely a key-order divergence. The float-metadata regression test in PR #70's branch uses alphabetical fixture keys so the number-formatting slice stays isolated; this issue tracks the ordering fix.
